By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 of 
the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows :

hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, 
ratification, or other action of the President, the authority conferred 
upon the President by the first section of the Act of July 3, 1926 (22 
U.S.C. 211a), to designate and prescribe for and on behalf of the 
United States rules governing the granting, issuing, and verifying of 
passports.

following are hereby superseded :
(1) Executive Order No. 7856 of March 31, 1938, entitled “Rules 
Governing the Granting and Issuing of Passports in the United 
States.”
(2) Executive Order No. 8820 of July 11,1941, entitled “Amending 
the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States.”
Sec. 3. Saving provisions.  All rules and regulations contained 
in the Executive order provisions revoked by Section 2 of this order, 
and all rules and regulations issued under the authority of those pro­
visions, which are in force at the time of the issuance of this order 
shall remain in full force and effect until revoked, or except as they 
may be hereafter amended or modified, in pursuance of the authority 
conferred by this order, unless sooner terminated by operation of law.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 authorizes the Civil Service Commission to confer a benefit provided by an Executive order on an employee or former employee who became ineligible solely because an agency erred or overlooked making a timely determination or recommendation, only after the agency makes it and not retroactively; section 2 denies appeal rights against personnel actions effective before the agency was notified of the grant; section 3 revokes Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954, a one-time command complete in 1959. Executive Order 12107 section 2-101 amended the clause by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Office for the Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404; before and after the change the authority is the same, and the amendment renames the actor. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, 5 CFR 351.502 still refers to cases under it, and its cited statutory authority survives in 5 U.S.C. 3301, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order restates Executive Order 8809 (as amended by 9323) as one paragraph establishing the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, with eligibility by three years of service from August 27, 1940, one year of wartime service after December 7, 1941, or shorter honorable service after June 27, 1950, and a proviso against awards for under one year except for service-incurred disability. Executive Order 14085 section 2 (87 FR 60541; no later effective date is stated, so the signing date October 3, 2022 is used) amended that restated text by striking men and inserting members and adding Space Force references on or after December 20, 2019; the amendment changes the persons covered but not the clause's continuation. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, the U.S. Code note still prints it as amended, and the order cites no authority statute that could lapse, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.
